Content: Over many generations, `text(two)` populations of the same species can diverge into separate species through reproductive isolation. The figures below represent a model of speciation and show the results of matings between individuals from `text(two)` diverging populations at `text(four)` different stages of speciation. The males represented in the model are heterogametic, which means they have `text(two)` different sex-determining chromosomes, (e.g., `text(XY)`). The females are homogametic, which means they have `text(two)` similar sex-determining chromosomes, (e.g., `text(XX)`). The offspring from each mating are labeled interpopulation hybrids.

Figure `1` shows the results of a mating between a male and a female from the `text(two)` populations. In each subsequent figure, the males are from `text(one)` of the diverging populations and the females are from the other population. The fertility and viability of the offspring from each mating are indicated in the figures.
